UPDATE - Bing has announced they will retire their search API on August 11th, 2025. Microsoft has encouraged users to migrate to their "Grounding with Bing Search" tool, however this is really only practical for use within the Azure AI Foundry ecosystem and is not intended for general use outside of Azure AI Agents. We recommend trying SerpApi's Bing Search API as a replacement for Bing's soon-to-be-retired API.

## Yahoo

Yahoo used to offer something called Yahoo Search BOSS, which included a BOSS JSON Search API. However they discontinued Search BOSS in 2016. They don't currently have anything like a web search API.

## DuckDuckGo

DuckDuckGo offers a DuckDuckGo Instant Answers API, however it only provides access to their Instant Answers, it is not a full web search API

results.title: Best Web Search APIs for AI Applications in 2026
results.content:
The web search API market has been changing dramatically with AI applications driving demand for smarter search capabilities. With Microsoft's decision to retire Bing Search APIs in August 2025, developers are evaluating web search API alternatives and discovering new platforms built specifically for AI workflows.

Our web search API comparison examines both traditional SERP APIs and AI-native search engines that power modern applications. Whether you need a search API for RAG systems, semantic search for AI agents, or reliable data extraction for business intelligence, choosing the right platform affects performance, functionality, and costs. [...] This guide covers the best web search APIs for developers in 2026, including detailed analysis of pricing, capabilities, and ideal use cases. We'll compare everything from enterprise-grade SerpAPI alternatives to specialized platforms like Firecrawl search, Exa, and Tavily that target specific AI workflows. By the end, we hope you find the best web search API for you and your applications.

## What is a Web Search API?

A web search API provides programmatic access to search engine results through HTTP requests, returning structured data in JSON or other machine-readable formats instead of visual web interfaces that we use for day-to-day web browsing.

### What are web search APIs used for?

results.title: 7 Best Bing Search API Alternatives and Replacements in 2026
results.content:
Web Search: standard organic search results.
 Image Search: image results and thumbnails.
 News Search: current news articles.
 Video Search: video results and metadata.
 Autosuggest: query suggestions as users type.
 Spell Check: spelling correction for queries.
 Entity Search: facts about people, places, and things.
 Custom Search: results scoped to sites you choose.
 Local Business Search: nearby places and listings.

One API key gave you all of it. That breadth is exactly what makes the shutdown hard to replace.

### Why Microsoft Retired It

Microsoft is moving search into AI agents instead of exposing a raw endpoint. The new idea is that search happens inside an AI assistant, not through a simple call your code controls. [...] Switching providers is a short, four-step job:

 Pick a provider: choose the category that fits your pipeline, then the tool.
 Swap endpoint and auth: point your code at the new URL and update the API key.
 Map response fields: line up the new JSON fields with what your app expects.
 Test: run a few live queries and confirm the output matches.

With Olostep you can run that test on the 500 free requests, using the same web search API call shown earlier. Send a Bing results URL to the Scrapes endpoint with the Bing parser, and you get normalized JSON back in one request — no scraper to build or maintain.

## Do You Still Need Bing Data at All?

It is fair to ask whether Bing is worth replacing. The direct API is gone, so dropping it would be the easy move. [...] Yes — third-party SERP APIs like Olostep, SerpApi, and Bright Data scrape Bing's public results and return them as structured JSON.

results.title: All You Need to Know About the Official Google Search API and an Alternative to It | by Darshan Khandelwal | Medium
results.content:
The official Google Custom Search JSON API works well for low to moderate usage where official access, clear documentation, and strict compliance are priorities.

However, as search data needs grow, be it in terms of volume, frequency, or SERP completeness, the limitations around daily caps, pricing, and flexibility become more noticeable.

In such cases, a third-party solution like Scrapingdog’s Google Search API can be a practical alternative, offering greater scalability and fewer operational constraints.

Before making a decision, it’s important to evaluate how much search data you need, how often you need it, and how critical flexibility and scale are for your workflow. Aligning these factors with the right API will help you build a more reliable and cost-effective solution. [...] ### 1. Create a Google Cloud project

The first step is to create a project in the Google Cloud Console. This project acts as the container where your API usage, quotas, and billing are managed. Every request made to the API is tied to this project.

### 2. Enable the Custom Search JSON API

Once the Cloud project is created, you must explicitly enable the Custom Search JSON API from the API Library. Without enabling the API, requests will not be processed, even if you have an API key.

### 3. Create a Programmable Search Engine (CX)

To use the API, you must create a Programmable Search Engine. This step is mandatory.

The Programmable Search Engine defines what content the API is allowed to search. You can configure it to:

 Search specific websites
 Or search a broader web scope [...] Here’s a video from our founder on using Scrapingdog’s Google Search API:-

The documentation here will help you to know how different parameters work.

You can even test it out on the playground when you sign up for the free pack. Unlike the official Google Custom Search JSON API, Scrapingdog does not impose a hard, fixed daily request cap that blocks usage once a threshold is reached.

Instead, usage is governed by credits and plan limits, which allows requests to scale smoothly based on actual demand. This makes it suitable for workloads that require continuous querying or higher daily volumes without abrupt interruptions.
